extracted.intended_audience: Users of TikZ/pgf (LaTeX/TeX) who draw diagrams and use path decorations, tree layouts, foreach loops, and calendar utilities
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for TikZ/pgf path decorations (snakes), to-paths and curve options, loop styles, tree growth/edge styles, the \foreach construct, and the pgfcalendar date/calendar utilities. It explains options, parameters, and example usage for producing diagrams and calendars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake expanding waves
rubrics_metrics.description: This snake adds arcs to the path that get bigger along the line towards the target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters: \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines the distance between consecutive arcs; \pgfsnakesegmentangle determines the opening angle below and above the path (total opening angle is twice this angle). Example usage: \draw[snake=expanding waves] (0,0) -- (3,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake saw
rubrics_metrics.description: This snake looks like the blade of a saw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters: \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines how much each spike raises above the straight line; \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines the length each spike. Example: \draw[snake=saw] (0,0) -- (3,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake snake (sine wave)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sine-wave-like snake with a 'softened' start and ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters: \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines the sine wave’s amplitude; \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines the sine wave’s wavelength. Example: \draw[snake=snake] (0,0) -- (3,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake ticks
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds straight lines (ticks) orthogonal to the line toward the target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters: \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines distance between consecutive ticks; \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines half the length of the ticks. Example: \draw[snake=ticks] (0,0) -- (3,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake triangles
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds triangles to the path that point toward the target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters: \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines distance between triangles; \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines half the length of the triangle side orthogonal to the path; \pgfsnakesegmentobjectlength determines the triangle height. Example: \draw[snake=triangles] (0,0) -- (3,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake crosses
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds diagonal crosses to the path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters: \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines distance between crosses; \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines half the height of each cross; \pgfsnakesgmentobjectlength determines the width of each cross. Example: \draw[snake=crosses] (0,0) -- (3,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake waves
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds arcs of constant size to the path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters: \pgfsnakesegmentlength sets distance between arcs; \pgfsnakesegmentangle sets opening angle below and above the path (total is twice this); \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines the radius of each arc. Example: \draw[snake=waves] (0,0) -- (3,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake zigzag
rubrics_metrics.description: Produces a zig-zag line along the path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters: \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude controls how much the zig-zag raises/falls from the straight line; \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines the length of a complete 'up-down' cycle. Example: \draw[snake=zigzag] (0,0) -- (3,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: style=line to
rubrics_metrics.description: Installs a to path that is a simple straight line from start to target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with to or edge operations: \draw (0,0) to[line to] (1,0);

rubrics_metrics.name: style=curve to (basic behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the to path to be a curve leaving the start at an out angle and reaching the target at an in angle; control point distances are computed in various ways depending on options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installing the curve to style allows options such as out=, in=, relative, controls=, looseness=, distance=, and explicit control coordinates. Several of these options implicitly enable curve to.

rubrics_metrics.name: out=(angle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies the angle at which the curve leaves the start coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the start is a node, the start coordinate is the point on the border at that angle; the control point lies at a computed distance in that direction. Example: [out=45] used in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: in=(angle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies the angle at which the curve reaches the target coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to out=; if target is a node, the target point is taken on border at given angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: relative=(true|false)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines whether in and out angles are absolute (relative to the paper) or relative to the straight line from start to target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative means measured relative to the straight line; e.g., relative out=30° bends left 30° from the straight line. Examples show differences and combined usage with out/in.

rubrics_metrics.name: bend left / bend right
rubrics_metrics.description: Convenience option that sets out and in angles to form a bend to one side (uses last given bend angle if none provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bend left=(angle) sets out=(angle), in=180-(angle), relative; bend right is symmetric. If no angle is given, the last bend angle is reused.

rubrics_metrics.name: bend angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the angle used by bend left/right globally without selecting curve to or relative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to globally specify a bend angle for a whole picture; does not alone enable curve behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: looseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies how 'loose' the curve will be by scaling the computed control-point distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TikZ computes the distance between start and target and multiplies by a fixed factor and by looseness. If looseness=1 (default) and in/out differ by 90°, a quarter circle results. Example comparisons shown (looseness=0.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: out looseness / in looseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the looseness factor for the out (start) or in (target) control distance individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you need different looseness on each side; they override the corresponding side's computed factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: min distance / max distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Set minimum and maximum distances for computed control-point distances; if computed d is below min it is replaced by min, if above max replaced by max.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These apply to the computed control-point distances from the start/target; used to clamp values to avoid extreme control points.

rubrics_metrics.name: out min distance / out max distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Set min/max only for the start (out) control distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows clamping the out control-point distance independently of the in side.

rubrics_metrics.name: in min distance / in max distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Set min/max only for the target (in) control distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows clamping the in control-point distance independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets both min and max distances to the same value, causing computed distance to be ignored and the specified distance to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forces fixed control-point distances; paired with examples: [out=45,in=135,distance=1cm].

rubrics_metrics.name: out distance / in distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the min and max out/in distance respectively (shorthand for out min/max and in min/max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience options to fix the distances used on either side.

rubrics_metrics.name: out control / in control
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify an explicit coordinate to be used as start/target control point (all distance computations ignored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts coordinates (including relative ones like +(1,0)). When used, computed d is ignored for that side.

rubrics_metrics.name: controls=(coord) and (coord)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide both control points explicitly to be used for the curve (computation ignored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw (0,0) to [controls=+(90:1) and +(90:1)] (3,0); This sets both control points directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=loop (loop behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: A loop to-path style similar to curve to but using the start as the target (i.e., loops back), with default looseness and min distance tuned for nice loops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences: actual target coordinate ignored, looseness is set to 8, min distance to 5mm by default (results in nice loops when opening angle is 30°). Use loop above/below/left/right to place the loop and node label correctly. The style every loop is installed at the beginning of every loop (default ->,shorten >=1pt).

rubrics_metrics.name: grow via three points (tree growth function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Growth function that places one-child at x, two children at y and z, and extrapolates positions for more children linearly from x,y,z using a formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parent has >2 children, positions placed at x + (n−1)/2 (y−x) + (c−1)(z−y), where n is number of children and c is index of current child. Useful to express a desired linear arrangement for arbitrary numbers of children; examples provided for several arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=grow cyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: Places children on a circle at distance \tikzleveldistance, using sibling angles instead of sibling distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: sibling angle=(angle) sets the angle between siblings; the function rotates children coordinate systems so grandchildren grow in the right direction. Examples show usage with nested levels and different level distances/angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: clockwise from / counterclockwise from
rubrics_metrics.description: Arranges children on a circle starting at a given angle and placing subsequent children by subtracting or adding the sibling angle in clockwise or counterclockwise order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: clockwise from=(angle) places the first child at angle and the next at angle - \tikzsiblingangle, and so on; it does NOT rotate the children's coordinate system (unlike grow cyclic).

rubrics_metrics.name: edge from parent fork down / right / left / up
rubrics_metrics.description: Styles to modify how edges from parent to children are drawn by first drawing a short orthogonal segment and then continuing horizontally/vertically to the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: edge from parent fork down draws a line downwards (half the level distance) and then horizontal/vertical to the child. Similar behavior for fork right/left/up; examples provided showing layout differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: \foreach basic syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: \foreach (variables) in {list} {commands} executes commands once per list item with variables set to current value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variables are usually a single TeX command (e.g., \x); list is comma-separated values; commands normally in braces. If no opening brace, commands scanned up to next semicolon. Nested \foreach statements can be written directly one after another and get treated as the commands for the outer loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: foreach semicolon and nested-foreach scanning behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If \foreach does not see an opening brace it scans up to the next semicolon for commands; if directly followed by another \foreach, the second is collected as the commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This behavior enables concise nested loops without braces, as shown in examples where a \foreach follows another directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: dots notation '...' in foreach lists
rubrics_metrics.description: The list item '...' expands to a sequence determined by preceding two numeric list items and the following bound; computes arithmetic progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules: with x,y,...,z, d=y−x, replaced by x,x+d,x+2d,... up to ≤z (or ≥z if d negative). Special case x,...,z (no y) sets d=1 or -1 depending on z> x. Examples illustrate integer and fractional steps; warning about rounding errors for fractional steps not multiples of 2^{-n}—recommend adjusting endpoints (e.g., use 0.501 instead of 0.5) for robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: special handling of pairs in foreach lists
rubrics_metrics.description: List items that are pairs like (0,1) contain commas internally; when an item starts with '(', everything up to the next ')' is part of the item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively wrap items containing commas in braces like {(0,1)}. This special handling makes iterating over coordinate pairs natural. Example: \foreach \position in {(0,0),(1,1)} \draw \position rectangle +(.25,.5);

rubrics_metrics.name: using foreach inside paths
rubrics_metrics.description: When a \foreach is used inside a path construction, the commands must be path construction commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show building paths dynamically with \foreach producing -- (x,y) fragments; also show using \foreach to generate multiple path segments inline.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiple variables (slash-separated) in foreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables can be a list separated by slashes (e.g., \x/\y) and list items then are slash-separated lists whose parts map to variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each execution assigns parts to variables; if an entry doesn't have enough slashes, the last entry is repeated. Examples: \foreach \x/\y in {1/2,a/b} yields '1 and 2','a and b'. Also supports nested data like {(0,0)/2mm} style entries for coordinates and sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: \breakforeach
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminates further executions of the current \foreach, but continues the current execution's commands normally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to exit loops early; recommended to use at end of a \foreach block. Example shows nested loops with conditional \breakforeach when \x<\y.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendardatetojulian (date input format rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts an ISO-format date string to a Julian day number in the Gregorian calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date format: year-month-day or year-month-last; year and month can be macros (\year, \month). Optionally append +N to add days. Examples: 2006-01-01, 2006-02-last, \year-\month-\day+1. Example conversion: \pgfcalendardatetojulian{2007-01-14}{\mycount} sets \mycount to 2454115.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendarjuliantodate (Julian → ISO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts a Julian day number to an ISO-date and assigns year/month/day into macros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned formats: year without leading zeros (can be 0), month is two-digit with leading zero, day is two-digit with leading zero. Example usage shows setting \isodate via the returned macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendarjuliantoweekday
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts a Julian day number to a weekday number (0 = Monday, 1 = Tuesday, ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \pgfcalendarjuliantoweekday{2454115}{\mycount} sets \mycount to 6 (Sunday).

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendarifdate tests and keys
rubrics_metrics.description: Execute code depending on properties/tests of an ISO-format date; tests are key-value pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default tests: all, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, workday (Mon–Fri), weekend (Sat/Sun), equals=(reference) (full or month-day), at least=, at most=, between=start and end, day of month=(number), end of month=(number, default 1). You can define new tests by adding keys to pgfcalendar; the key code should set \ifpgfcalendarmatches true when appropriate and can read macros like \pgfcalendarifdatejulian, \pgfcalendarifdateweekday, \pgfcalendarifdateyear, \pgfcalendarifdatemonth, \pgfcalendarifdateday. Example provided for defining a 'workers day' (May 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: weekday and month name macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Macros to obtain textual representations for weekdays and months given numeric indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \pgfcalendarweekdayname{n} expands to weekday name (0=Monday) in current language; \pgfcalendarweekdayshortname gives abbreviated name; \pgfcalendarmonthname{m} and \pgfcalendarmonthshortname{m} do the same for months. Example: \pgfcalendarweekdayname{2} yields Wednesday.

rubrics_metrics.name: localization of date text (translator package)
rubrics_metrics.description: All textual representations of weekdays/months are wrapped with \translate commands from the translator package and will be translated if translator (and translator-months-dictionary) is loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translator is not loaded, no translation occurs. The package will try to load translator-months-dictionary when translator is present; consult translator docs for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendar typesetting macro and rendering code contract
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfcalendar{prefix}{start}{end}{rendering code} enumerates dates from start to end and executes rendering code for each date with helper macros set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rendering code must position/produce output for each date and can assume accumulated settings across calls. Available helper macros inside rendering code: \pgfcalendarprefix, \pgfcalendarbeginiso, \pgfcalendarbeginjulian, \pgfcalendarendiso, \pgfcalendarendjulian, \pgfcalendarcurrentjulian, \pgfcalendarcurrentweekday. The rendering code is not grouped by default, so state can accumulate between dates; designers should handle positioning and node naming (use prefix recommended).
